failures.evidence: Source facts: (a) release tag pi-legion-envoy-v1.20.0 = 384dc5ee6629, committer 2026-09-13T06:06:12Z, parent 19b99c3c7db5 (#993, LEGION-33); `jj log -r '::pi-legion-envoy-v1.20.0 & description(glob:"*(#992)*")'` → 0 commits — LEGION-54's merge b3f5870a944c (#992, committer 06:04:08Z) is NOT an ancestor; pi-legion-envoy-v1.20.1 = 6312ef9791d0 (06:09:10Z) is the first tag that contains it (1 match). The two merges raced the release workflow two minutes apart. (b) `npm pack @sjawhar/pi-legion-envoy@1.20.0` → dist/legion.js: `LEGION_GRANT_FILE` 0 occurrences, `LEGION_GRANT` 2 (`LEGION_GRANT: grantId` inside the bash tool's env — the 1.17.1 env delivery the secretsd shim drops); 1.20.1 → `LEGION_GRANT_FILE` 4 occurrences incl. `LEGION_GRANT_FILE is not set on this pane`; 1.21.0, 1.21.1, 1.22.0, 1.22.1, 1.22.2, 1.23.0, 1.23.1 → 4 each. (c) `jj file show -r pi-legion-envoy-v1.20.0 packages/pi-envoy/CHANGELOG.md | grep -c LEGION_GRANT_FILE` → 0; at v1.20.1 → 1. (d) main's own record: 5aadcf2becfc 'docs: LEGION-54 shipped as pi-legion-envoy 1.20.1 (#1019)'; and this PR's Deployment section says 'Releases 1.20.1 through 1.22.2 carry contract 1'. Correct statement: 1.20.1 through 1.22.2 are the LEGION-54 builds that write the credential file; 1.20.0 declares 1 and still delivers the grant through the bash tool's env (so, like 1.14.0–1.19.0, it would have run workers that fail at their first credentialed command had the gate let it through). Fix: one token in two files ('1.20.0' → '1.20.1' in the parenthetical; 'before 1.20.0' → 'before 1.20.1'), plus the PR-body Summary bullet; the reviewer's thread-2 premise ('1.20.0 was released 06:06Z from a commit that contains it') was itself wrong and its thread reply should say so.
